STOCKS AND SOUPS

A pot of soup simmering on the stove epitomizes home cooking.

ABOUT MEAT AND POULTRY STOCKS

There is a strange irony to stock making.

BROWN BEEF STOCK

About 8 cups

Please read About Meat and Poultry Stocks. For a White Beef Stock, follow the directions for White Veal Stock.

Preheat the oven to 425°F. Place in a lightly oiled roasting pan and roast for 15 minutes:

  • 5 pounds meaty beef bones

Add:

  • 2 medium unpeeled onions, quartered
  • 2 carrots, cut into 2-inch pieces
  • 2 celery ribs, cut into 2-inch pieces

Roast, stirring occasionally, until the bones are well browned, about 40 minutes. Transfer to a stockpot. Carefully pour off the fat from the roasting pan and add:

  • 2 cups water or 1 cup white wine

Scrape up any browned bits, then pour the deglazed liquid into the stockpot. Add:

  • 1 leek, halved lengthwise, well cleaned, and cut into 2-inch pieces
  • 3 or 4 sprigs parsley
  • 2 or 3 sprigs thyme
  • 1 bay leaf
  • ¼ teaspoon white or black peppercorns
  • (2 whole cloves)

Add:

  • Cold water to cover

Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat and simmer, partially covered, for 6 to 8 hours. Skim off any impurities that rise to the surface during the first hour of cooking and add water as needed to keep the ingredients covered. Strain and cool uncovered, then refrigerate covered.

WHITE VEAL STOCK

About 8 cups

Please read About Meat and Poultry Stocks.

Combine in a stockpot:

  • 4 to 5 pounds veal knuckles or meaty bones
  • Cold water to cover

Bring to a boil over high heat and blanch the veal bones for a few minutes to remove impurities. Drain again and add:

  • 1 unpeeled onion, coarsely chopped
  • 3 celery ribs, coarsely chopped
  • 1 carrot, coarsely chopped

Once more, add:

  • Cold water to cover

Bring to a boil, then simmer for 6 to 8 hours. Strain and cool.

TOOLS FOR MAKING STOCK

The best stockpots are narrow, tall, and heavy-bottomed.
